key_insight: RubriQ turns quantum circuit synthesis into an LLM code-generation problem and uses rubric-guided GRPO to optimize circuits for fidelity, T-gate reduction, and hardware compatibility.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a scalable HPC-enabled path to producing fault-tolerant, hardware-ready quantum circuits with minimal constraint violations for real devices.
method: LLM generates candidate quantum circuits as code.
Programmatic rubric scores T-gate count, topology compliance, and unitary fidelity as the RL reward.
CUDA-Q simulation and DeepSpeed ZeRO2 enable fast multi-node training on A100 clusters.
evidence_signal: In benchmark tests, RubriQ achieved 3.31x mean T-gate compression versus 2.05x for sparse-reward RL, converged 2-3x faster, and kept hardware-constraint violations below 1% while validating on IBM and IonQ hardware.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate rubric design and simulation-in-the-loop training, so reward mis-specification or simulator-to-hardware mismatch could limit real-world transfer.
paper_title: RubriQ: Rubric-Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization for Constraint-Aware Quantum Circuit Synthesis
